record.original_question: For two-dimensional hydrodynamics on D_mu^s(M), what is the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic from the identity, and is the existence of conjugate points related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows on M?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of Sobolev-class $H^s$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (with $s>2$), equipped with the right-invariant weak $L^2$ Riemannian metric whose value at the identity is the $L^2$ inner product of divergence-free vector fields. Geodesics of this metric starting at the identity correspond to solutions of the Euler equations for an ideal incompressible fluid on $M$. A point $\eta(t_0)$ along such a geodesic $\eta:[0,T)\to\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ is called conjugate to the identity if the differential of the Riemannian exponential map $d\exp_e$ at $t_0\dot\eta(0)$ fails to be an isomorphism.

(a) Determine the order (i.e., the dimension of the kernel of $d\exp_e$, counted with multiplicity) of the first conjugate point along an arbitrary $L^2$ geodesic from the identity in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$.

(b) Determine whether the existence of conjugate points along the geodesic generated by a stationary solution of the Euler equations on $M$ is related to (in particular, implied by or equivalent to the failure of) Arnold's stability criterion for that stationary flow.
artifact.category_tag: Infinite-dimensional Riemannian geometry of diffeomorphism groups
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: Ebin–Misiołek–Preston showed that the first conjugate point on the volumorphism group is always pathological (the differential of the exponential map fails to be Fredholm), and Misiołek–Preston studied the exponential map near such points. Arnold originally conjectured a link between positive curvature, conjugate points, and stability. However, no general answer determining the order of the first conjugate point on a 2D volumorphism group along an arbitrary geodesic, nor a precise equivalence between conjugate-point existence and Arnold stability, has been established; this is listed as an open problem in the Khesin–Misiołek–Modin problem collection.

status_evidence.title: On the Volumorphism Group, the First Conjugate Point is Always the Hardest
status_evidence.snippet: The first conjugate point along a geodesic in the volumorphism group is always pathological: the differential of the exponential map fails to be Fredholm.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result on the nature of the first conjugate point in the volumorphism group.

status_evidence.title: The Exponential Map Near Conjugate Points In 2D Hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: The weak-Riemannian exponential map of the L² metric on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a compact two-dimensional manifold is not injective in any neighbourhood of its conjugate vectors.
status_evidence.claim: Studies behavior of the exponential map near conjugate points in 2D, indicating the question of order/relation to stability is still investigated.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 19. Conjugate points and Arnold stability.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in the collection.
